Alex H: Quick Q — I switched from full-time to part-time in Feb and then back to full-time in May. I was on the HDHP Jan–Apr, then non-HDHP May onward. Can I still contribute to the HSA for the whole year or is it prorated? Also, our payroll vendor migrated in March — I noticed my 401k match for Feb appeared late in April. How do we make sure matches are credited to the right pay periods?

Priya (People Ops): Short answers: HSA eligibility is based on your HDHP status on Dec 1 for the last-month rule OR the actual number of months you were eligible. We can run the "last-month rule" check for you and see if you need to do a pro-rata exception. For 401k match timing, Marco — can you confirm how the vendor migration handles retro matches?

Marco (Payroll): Hi — during vendor cutover we batched a few runs which caused match postings to land on the next payroll cycle. We can make retro adjustments to attribute match to original pay period in the records, but the tax year / paycheck timing stays as posted. If Alex wants the match reported to a specific pay period for reconciliation, we need a ticket + signed consent.

Alex H: Ok — I care because my W-2 / year-to-date looks odd and I was close to the catch-up limit (turning 50 in Nov). If match posting in April bumps any deferral limits, will that affect catch-up eligibility?

Jenna Benefits: Matches don't count against employee elective deferral limits, but they do count toward the overall annual addition limit. For 401k catch-up (age 50+) the extra elective deferral is based on actual deferrals withheld. If you elect catch-up starting the month you turn 50, it won't be retroactively applied unless payroll does a retro pay adjustment with appropriate forms. Suggest we review your deferral history and see if a retro payroll entry is needed.

Alex H: Got it. For HSA — is there any paperwork to elect a pro-rata contribution or to opt into the last-month rule?

Priya (People Ops): We have a short form for the HSA testing/last-month rule. I'll DM you the PDF. If you opt into last-month rule but then become ineligible in the following 12 months, you'd need to withdraw excess contributions or be taxed. If you prefer, we can calculate the pro-rated max and submit adjustments to payroll.

Marco (Payroll): To fix the match attribution we need: a) Alex cc's Priya on the ticket, b) signed authorization for retro allocation, and c) payroll window ID to adjust. Once submitted we can run an off-cycle to correct YTD reporting. Timing: allow ~2 weeks for vendor processing.

HR-Bot: Reminder: 2026 HSA individual limit = $3,850, family = $7,750. Catch-up contribution for 50+ = $1,000. See benefits.redwood.com/limits for details. :calendar:

Alex H: Thanks everyone — Priya I'll take the form, Marco I'll open a ticket with the payroll window ID. One last ask: if I switch between HDHP and non-HDHP midyear again, is there a simple worksheet I can use to estimate my allowed HSA contribution?

Jenna Benefits: Yes — there's a worksheet (spreadsheet) in the benefits drive that walks month-by-month eligibility and pro-rata limits. I'll add you and Priya to permissions and drop the link in this thread.

Priya (People Ops): Adding the forms & worksheet now. Alex — once you sign the HSA election/last-month rule form and the payroll retro consent we'll coordinate with Marco and Benefits to reconcile everything. :thumbsup:
